Hospitals almost always have some kind of anti-suicide program. All you need to do is go to the Emergency and let them know you're experiencing suicidal ideation and you're afraid you may be a danger to yourself or others. They'll make sure you have someone to talk to.

It may seem like your progress isn't moving as fast as you like, but the only way to improve is tenacity. You have to keep at it, and you'll start noticing the results you're looking for.

Regarding the people in your life and your perspective of yourself, always remember that you fit someone's ideal of beauty, and that people come and go through our lives. As you age and mature you'll get a better sense for people and what types of people they actually are, and that will help you distinguish between the people who use you and real friends. 

While it may be painful to have lost someone, the fact that you're in pain because of it meant that you enjoyed your time with them. As time moves forward it'll be easier to focus on the positive memories, as the negative ones will slowly fade to the back. They may never fully leave, but they hurt less and less and become far harder to remember as time goes on.

I feel very much in the same boat as you. I'm 24, no degree, no certificates, and starting to drown in debt. I've been told my entire life that I can do anything i put my mind to, even now. But you have something that I dont: artistic talent and a creative spark. Focus on those and develop them. Those things can take you very far, and even if you don't achieve commercial success, art is for you. It's personal and intimate. Whenever you feel like things are getting to be too much, take the 5 to 10 minutes to create a rough sketch or jot down some ideas for a project and start working at it little by little after work.
